title: Simultaneous generically finite flatification over integral etale charts
statement: Let $X$ be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], meaning it has a finite affine cover by Noetherian rings, whose affine coordinate rings are quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Let $(e_i:E_i\to X)_{i\in I}$ be a finite family of separated etale morphisms of finite type with nonempty integral sources [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. No covering hypothesis is imposed. For each $i$ let $f_i:F_i\to E_i$ be proper and dominant with $F_i$ integral and with finite function field extension of degree $n_i=[k(F_i):k(E_i)]>0$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]; dominant means dense image and function field means the local ring at the generic point. Then there exist a normal integral Noetherian scheme $X'$, a proper morphism $p:X'\to X$ that is an isomorphism over a dense open of $X$, and, writing $E_i'=E_i\times_X X'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], integral Noetherian schemes $F_i'$ with finite locally free surjections $a_i:F_i'\to E_i'$ of constant rank $n_i$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free, def-weil-surjective-morphism], together with $E_i$-morphisms $F_i'\to F_i$. Each $E_i'$ is integral and normal, its projection $E_i'\to E_i$ induces an isomorphism of function fields, and $F_i'\to F_i$ also induces an isomorphism of function fields. All these schemes are of finite type over $X$. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. The schemes $F_i'$ may be chosen as the scheme-theoretic closures of the generic fibres of $F_i$ in $F_i\times_X X'$: on an affine open this closure is cut out by the kernel of restriction to that generic fibre [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure].
